title: refactor(ci): modernize build matrix, cache parallelism, and release automation
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Our CI runtime and release automation have grown brittle and slow as the repo and test surface expanded. This PR consolidates and modernizes the GitHub Actions workflows, improves cache parallelism and cache key hygiene, and fixes a few release automation race conditions.

What this PR does:
- Unifies and simplifies the main CI build matrix (node/python/go) while splitting heavy integration tests into a separate 'integration' job group that can be scaled independently.
- Reworks cache keys to use shard-aware keys and restores with fallback keys to improve cache hit rates under parallelism.
- Adds concurrency groups and cancel-in-progress to reduce wasted runs when pushes are frequent.
- Updates release workflow to wait for required checks explicitly and handle transient failures in the publish step (retries + idempotency).
- Bumps GH Actions to current stable versions (actions/checkout@v4, actions/cache@v4, pnpm/action-setup@v3, etc.) and consolidates duplicated workflow logic into reusable workflow_call templates.
- Adds a small helper script (tools/ci/cache-utils.sh) used to compute deterministic cache keys and shard IDs for matrix parallelism.

Checklist:
- [x] CI builds pass locally and in GH Actions
- [x] Integration tests run in separate job and are flakey-tolerant with retries
- [x] Release dry-run verified against staging registry
- [x] Docs updated (docs/ci.md) with new matrix semantics and migration notes

Migration notes for maintainers: update repository automations that reference the old workflow filenames (.github/workflows/*) to the new consolidated entrypoints or workflow_call templates. If you maintain a long-running branch that pins action versions, please update to actions/checkout@v4 and actions/cache@v4 to avoid cache incompatibilities.

Impact: No runtime or customer-facing product changes. Expected CI wall time reduction ~25-35% for PRs with medium changes due to improved caching and reduced redundant runs. Integration tests can be scaled independently when needed.

diff_snippets:
--- a/.github/workflows/ci.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
@@ -1,8 +1,20 @@
-uses: actions/checkout@v2
+uses: actions/checkout@v4
+concurrency: 
+  group: ${{ github.ref }}-ci
+  cancel-in-progress: true

--- a/.github/workflows/ci.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
@@ -20,7 +32,13 @@
 matrix: 
-  node: [16,18]
+  include: 
+    - node: 18
+      label: fast
+    - node: 20
+      label: modern
+cache: 
+  key: ${{ runner.os }}-ci-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}

--- a/tools/ci/cache-utils.sh
+++ b/tools/ci/cache-utils.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# small helper to compute deterministic cache keys and shard ids for GH matrix parallelism
+set -euo pipefail
+echo "CI_CACHE_KEY=$(date +%Y%m%d)-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)-shard-$1"

Ava Chen (2026-02-26): Reply: switched to workflow_call templates for shared logic; added shard-aware cache keys in tools/ci/cache-utils.sh and updated restore-keys fallback to avoid collisions.

Ivy Patel (2026-02-27): Requested changes: please add a short doc in docs/ci.md explaining shard calculation and update Makefile.ci targets that consumers use in CI debugging. Also add a small unit test for cache-utils.sh (mocked).
Ava Chen (2026-02-28): Addressed: added docs entry, added basic shellcheck-compatible test under tools/ci/test-cache-utils.sh, and updated Makefile.ci with 'ci-debug' target.
Morgan Lee (2026-03-01): Approval: Looks good. Verified a couple of sample PRs show improved cache hits and the release retry fixed the flake we saw in last week's incident.
